These comparisons use recognizable public resources: compcodeR simulations,
the airway RNA-seq experiment, the Schurch yeast replicate study, and the
original OUTRIDER Kremer/GTEx-skin count backgrounds. Native method fits are
preserved byte-for-byte and WADE is recomputed with the migrated public API.
The [original reference protocol](../archive/development-20260923/docs/reference-benchmark-plan.md) records
versions, sources, exclusions and the custom outlier injections.

The purpose is an honest comparison of capabilities and limitations. WADE is
intended to complement conventional DE in large cohorts, not replace DESeq2
in small studies. Gene-level distribution tests and sample-gene outlier tests
must retain their distinct hypotheses and multiple-testing families.

## Conventional differential expression

Unmodified compcodeR generation uses three replicates per sample size. The
raw-count eligibility/reference universe is preserved from the native fit,
and RLE factor parity is checked. WADE uses 49,999 shuffles, seed 20260919,
no noise and one distribution q-value. Native DESeq2 and edgeR retain their
own fitting and filtering behavior. Larger gene families have a p-value floor
of 2e-5 at this cap, so isolated discoveries can be unresolved.

```{python}
#| label: reference-tables
reference,reference_source=CS.load(ROOT,"reference",OUT)
outlier,outlier_source=CS.load(ROOT,"outlier",OUT)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-reference-power
#| fig-cap: "Conventional compcodeR mean changes. All requested DE genes, including generator/test-filter losses, remain in the power denominator. Three matrices per size provide limited precision."
sim=reference[reference.dataset.str.startswith("compcodeR")]
summary=CS.summary(sim,["method","n_case"],"power")
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(7,3.8),layout="constrained")
for method,color in CS.COLORS.items():
    part=summary[summary.method==method].sort_values("n_case")
    if len(part):
        ax.plot(part.n_case,part["mean"],"o-",color=color,label=method)
        ax.fill_between(part.n_case,part.lo,part.hi,color=color,alpha=.12)
ax.set(xlabel="Samples per group",ylabel="Requested DE genes recovered",ylim=(0,1))
ax.legend()
export_table(CS.as_polars(summary),OUT,"reference-power-summary")
fig
```

Airway and Schurch are real count matrices with known experimental labels;
they do not provide comprehensive independent per-gene truth. Call counts or
agreement on these data are not sensitivity/specificity estimates. Airway's
paired donor design is preserved through within-donor label swaps.

## OUTRIDER and related methods

The native competitors are OUTRIDER's autoencoder, its PCA alternative, saseR,
and OutSingle. Their sample-gene outputs remain visible. OutSingle supplies
scores without native p-values. For a gene-level comparison, native p-values
are aggregated over case samples by a conservative Bonferroni minimum-p
operation and then BH across genes. This aggregation asks a different question
from a cohort distribution test and does not become a native OUTRIDER gene test.

Injected patterns on the original count backgrounds are our controlled pilot,
not a reproduction of every published injection scheme. Global changes and
mixed bulk mechanisms are evaluated as group alterations rather than insisting
that a latent-factor outlier model call every shifted cell an outlier.
Unmodified real cells are not known negatives. Consequently, calls outside the
planted targets are reported as such, not mislabeled false discoveries.

```{python}
#| label: outlier-tables
native=pd.read_csv(outlier_source/"native-scores.tsv",sep="\t")
group=pd.read_csv(outlier_source/"group-scores.tsv",sep="\t")
```

```{python}
#| label: native-outlier-recall
#| output: asis
table(native[["background","method","changed_cells","changed_cell_recall","apparent_cell_average_precision"]],"native-outlier-summary",
    {"background":"Background","method":"Method","changed_cells":"Changed cells",
     "changed_cell_recall":"Cell recall","apparent_cell_average_precision":"Apparent AP"})
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-outlier-gene-recall
#| fig-cap: "Gene-level recovery of injected upward patterns, split by real count background. Native case-minP aggregation and WADE distribution tests retain different hypotheses. The horizontal axis uses the selected case count; multiplying zero counts can leave some targets unchanged. One injection matrix per background does not supply a replicated calibration study."
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(10,4),layout="constrained",sharey=True)
colors=dict(CS.COLORS,**{"OUTRIDER-AE case-minP":"#775aa5","OUTRIDER-PCA case-minP":"#af91ce",
                         "saseR case-minP":"#4e923c"})
for ax,background in zip(axes,["kremer","gtex-skin"]):
    part=group[(group.background==background)&(group.pattern=="up")]
    for method in part.method.unique():
        rows=part[part.method==method].sort_values("realized_prevalence")
        ax.plot(rows.realized_prevalence,rows.recall,"o-",ms=3,label=method,color=colors[method])
    ax.set(title=background,xlabel="Selected case fraction",ylim=(0,1))
axes[0].set_ylabel("Altered genes recovered")
handles,labels=axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(handles,labels,loc="outside upper center",ncol=3,fontsize=8)
export_table(CS.as_polars(group),OUT,"outlier-group-results")
fig
```

## Release interpretation

The [sample-size notebook](benchmark.qmd) shows the larger replicated pattern
screen. The [transcriptome confirmation](../archive/development-20260923/docs/transcriptome-workflow-validation.md)
addresses full gene families, filtering, reference overlap and correlation in
its stated bulk scope. Neither dataset choice nor a successful fit certifies
universal FDR control. Sparse workflows, depth-confounded comparisons and
predictive rare-event significance retain separate open research requirements.
All tables, plots and conclusions here are pending approval.
